For symmetric positive definite \(A\), the norm is controlled eigenvalue-by-eigenvalue. Thus

\[
\rho(p_1,p_2)=\max_{x\in [1,2]\cup[8,16]}
\left|\frac{(x-p_1)(x-p_2)}{(x+p_1)(x+p_2)}\right|.
\]

Write

\[
S=p_1+p_2,\qquad P=p_1p_2.
\]

Then the scalar rational function is

\[
r(x)=\frac{x^2-Sx+P}{x^2+Sx+P}.
\]

For a target \(q\), the condition \(|r(x)|\le q\) for all \(x\in E\) is equivalent to

\[
\alpha\max_{x\in E}\left(x+\frac Px\right)\le S
\le
\alpha^{-1}\min_{x\in E}\left(x+\frac Px\right),
\qquad
\alpha=\frac{1-q}{1+q}.
\]

So we need maximize

\[
\frac{\min_E (x+P/x)}{\max_E (x+P/x)}.
\]

Using only the four endpoints,

\[
\min_E\left(x+\frac Px\right)
\le \min\left(2+\frac P2,\;8+\frac P8\right),
\]

and

\[
\max_E\left(x+\frac Px\right)
\ge \max\left(1+P,\;16+\frac P{16}\right).
\]

For \(P\le 16\), this gives

\[
\frac{\min}{\max}\le
\frac{2+P/2}{16+P/16}\le \frac{10}{17},
\]

with equality only at \(P=16\). For \(P\ge16\),

\[
\frac{\min}{\max}\le
\frac{8+P/8}{1+P}\le \frac{10}{17},
\]

again with equality only at \(P=16\).

Thus \(P=16\). Then

\[
x+\frac{16}{x}\in[10,17]
\]

on both intervals, and

\[
r(x)=\frac{x+16/x-S}{x+16/x+S}.
\]

The minimax choice balances the endpoint errors:

\[
\frac{S-10}{S+10}=\frac{17-S}{17+S}.
\]

This gives

\[
S^2=170,\qquad S=\sqrt{170}.
\]

Hence \(p_1,p_2\) are the roots of

\[
t^2-\sqrt{170}\,t+16=0,
\]

so

\[
p_1=\frac{\sqrt{170}-\sqrt{106}}{2},
\qquad
p_2=\frac{\sqrt{170}+\sqrt{106}}{2}.
\]

The minimum contraction factor is

\[
\frac{\sqrt{170}-10}{\sqrt{170}+10}.
\]

Final answer:

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{\sqrt{170}-\sqrt{106}}{2},\frac{\sqrt{170}+\sqrt{106}}{2}\right)}
\]
